predict.prompt: Predict the decisive experimental condition before fully solving: Represent 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O before reaction, as hot vapour and after complete condensation.
predict.defensible_answer: Under the ideal-gas approximation, equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles for comparable gas mixtures. This underlies the use of gaseous volume ratios from balanced reaction coefficients when all reacting and measured species remain gases at the same reference T/P. For example, 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g) gives two gas-volume units H₂ and one O₂ forming two units of water vapour at comparable conditions. If water condenses, the measured gas volume is no longer two units.

predict.defensible_answer: Gas collection by water displacement is convenient for relatively insoluble gases, but the collection may include water vapour. predict.prompt: Predict the decisive experimental condition before fully solving: Represent methane combustion inventory before heating, while water is vapour, and after cooling, assuming excess O₂.
predict.defensible_answer: For complete combustion of a hydrocarbon containing only carbon and hydrogen, the usual products are carbon dioxide and water. The general balanced formula for CₓHᵧ under sufficient oxygen is CₓHᵧ + (x + y/4)O₂ → xCO₂ + (y/2)H₂O. This equation conserves atoms, but the gas state of H₂O depends on temperature. High-temperature water vapour can condense when cooled, removing water molecules from the measured gas phase without removing them from the closed material system.

predict.prompt: Predict the decisive experimental condition before fully solving: Represent each stage of the example 10 mL CH₄ + 30 mL O₂ after reaction, cooling and CO₂ absorption.
predict.defensible_answer: Eudiometry is a multi-stage gas-volume analysis, generally beyond ordinary Class X Chemistry and therefore marked **ENRICHMENT**. A typical process combines a known gas with oxygen, burns it in a controlled apparatus, cools to a chosen reference condition, selectively absorbs a product such as CO₂ and measures residual volumes. The inference depends on knowing what each stage removes. A gas-volume drop after cooling may include water condensation, while a later reduction with suitable CO₂ absorber is attributed to carbon dioxide under validated selectivity.
